business: NOCTIS, a smart bedside companion by offhours (EUR 120)
why_not: I already have a smart display that does alarm, weather and calendar, and it cost me less. I've never actually moved my phone out of the bedroom, so I doubt a EUR 120 object would be what changes that.

I keep my phone within reach because of the kids and emergencies, so something that replaces it at the bedside solves a problem I don't have. I already have an alarm that works, even if I snooze it too much.
EUR 120 is a lot when my phone already does the alarm and the weather for free. I like how it looks, but I'd be paying a lot to fix a habit I've already failed to fix with willpower.
EUR 120 is a lot when my phone already does the alarm and the weather for free. I'd rather wait for a sale or buy a 25 euro sunrise lamp on Amazon.

I know I scroll too long at night, but I'd still keep my phone on the bedside table for emergencies, so this would just be a second gadget next to it. Screen-time limits haven't stuck for me and I don't believe a nicer alarm clock changes that.
It looks lovely, but I have never managed to leave my phone in another room, and my phone alarm already works and costs nothing. I would be paying 120 euros for a habit change I have not made yet.

My phone alarm works and I already own a watch for sleep stuff, so this has to be rock solid to replace it. I'd be nervous betting my morning on a new small-batch gadget, and 120 is a lot for a pre-order of something I can't try.

I already have a smart speaker and display, and I'm not putting another always-listening microphone next to my bed. My phone alarm works fine, even if I snooze it too much, and 120 euro for a better alarm clock is a lot.
flip: Proof that real people actually leave the phone in another room with it, plus a reliable way to still get emergency calls through to the bedside.
A price near EUR 60 to 70, or proof that it works with my existing smart-home setup instead of sitting beside it.
If it could reliably let urgent calls from the kids or family through without the phone being in the room, and cost around 70 euros.
If it could reliably let a call from family or the kids' school ring through while the phone sits in another room, and I could see it working for a few weeks first, I'd reconsider.
